ops.title: Decide the Unicode-version policy for the generated tokenizer table before CPython 3.14 support
ops.description:
The v12 lexicon tokenizer pins Python str.isalpha semantics into rust/src/generated/unicode.rs (660 ranges, Unicode 15.1.0 per the generated header). The abi3-py313 wheel runs unmodified on future CPython versions whose isalpha tables will differ (Python bumps Unicode most releases), so a prebuilt wheel on 3.14+ could tokenize differently in Rust vs that interpreter's Python fallback for newly-(re)classified codepoints.

Development-time drift IS alarmed: tests/test_literals_parity.py regenerates unicode.rs under the running interpreter and diffs (scripts/build_rust_literals.py:202 renders it live; the header embeds unicodedata.unidata_version) — CI on a newer Python fails loudly. The gap is only end users running the prebuilt wheel on a newer interpreter.

Decide when 3.14 support lands (surfaced by the codex diff review of b2d2b552): (a) regenerate the table per supported-Python bump and document "tokenizer follows the oldest supported CPython's Unicode tables"; (b) add a CI job on Python prereleases so the freshness gate fires early; (c) cap requires-python per release. Practical risk today is negligible (English coding transcripts; divergences are exotic codepoints).

ops.text: A documented policy exists for how unicode.rs tracks CPython Unicode versions across supported Pythons
